newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine firm can buy 42 pct in Ukraine pipe maker.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine firm can buy 42 pct in Ukraine pipe maker.

text.p: Ukraine's Anti-Monopoly Committee has allowed a Ukrainian company and its Ukrainian-U.S. joint venture subsidiary to purchase a 42 percent stake in a large rolled-steel pipe manufacturer, a spokesman said.

Interpipe Corporation and its joint-venture Bipe Co Ltd will be allowed to buy the shares in AT Nyzhnedniprovsky Truboprokratny Zavod (NTZ) in the eastern industrial city of Dnipropetrovsk, the committee's spokesman Yuri Varvynetz said.
He did not name the U.S. partner.
Interpipe executive Dmytro Bilokur, in a telephone interview on Thursday from the company's Dnipropetrovsk base, would not comment on the committee's announcement.
Varvynetz declined to say how much Interpipe already owns in NTZ, but said the Bipe Company was allowed to purchase 6.58 percent in the pipe manufacturer in August.
Brokers said the company was also able to buy 10.81 percent from two investment companies.
The workers' collective has rights to 78.1 percent of the shares, and managers have rights to 4.5 percent.
Buyers are obligated to invest $1.5 million by 1998 to modernise the factory, also located in Dnipropetrovsk.
Anatoly Yarlyk, the plant's deputy executive, said privatisation of NTZ was almost finished and that Interpipe would be the largest shareholder in the pipe manufacturer.
Metal pipes are one of Ukraine's largest export products.
